Honestly, it comes down to what tight end options you have on your roster outside of him. Is Philly a good matchup for tight ends? Hell no, but IF Ben Johnson wants to utilize Loveland, he has the talent to overcome a bad matchup. The question is: does Ben Johnson want to change things and get back to utilizing his best players? I don't know. Philly has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Ordonde Gadsden will step into a bigger role moving forward, with David Njoku and Charlie Kolar sidelined for the foreseeable future due to injuries. This season, he's only been a part-time player with a 28.8% route share, a 21% target-per-route run rate, 2.63 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 10.5% first-read share. Gadsden could return nice production moving forward if this offense gets rolling, but I'm not looking to start him this week. Buffalo has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Terrance Ferguson exploded as the TE8 for the week. Yes, Puka Nacua was out, but that's the exact scenario for this week as well. Through three quarters of last week's game, Ferguson was a full-time player (before the score got out of hand). In the first three quarters against the Giants, Ferguson had a 66.7% snap rate, a 71.4% route share, a 26.9% target share, 2.0 YPRR, and a 23.8% first-read share. Ferguson is a strong TE1 again this week. Denver has allowed the fourth-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Pat Freiermuth is the TE12 in fantasy points per game. He has a 12.3% target share, 1.37 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 10.2% first-read share. None of those numbers are amazing, but Freiermuth could easily flirt with TE1 numbers this week. Cincy has continued their struggles against tight ends this season. Dalton Schultz ripped them apart last week. Cincy has allowed the ninth-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.

What a massive bounceback week for Jake Ferguson in Week 2. He opened the season as the TE44 in weekly scoring, only to finish as TE4 last week. The concerning thing in his usage, though, is the fact that his route share fell from 69.4% to 55.6%, but it's only a one-game sample, so I'm not going to freak out. Last week, he did see a 12.9% target share with two of his four targets coming in the red zone. His touchdown equity in this offense remains substantial, but his market share of the passing offense isn't wonderful. Last week, Ferguson did finish with 43 receiving yards (2.15 YPRR), but he had only a 13.6% first-read share. He is a serviceable touchdown-dependent streamer, though. Baltimore ranks 15th in yards per target against tight ends while giving up the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. If Ferguson scores this week, you'll likely be happy that you streamed him, but if he is held out of the endzone expect frustration and tears.

Kyle Pitts has been an afterthought to begin the season. Yes, this is partially because of the Falcons' quarterback situation, but also because Pitts has only had a 50% snap share and 56.9% route share. Neither of those usage metrics was what I expected entering this season. I figured he would be an every-down player for Atlanta, especially considering the state of their receiving depth chart. Pitts has a 7.4% target share, 0.41 YPRR, zero red zone targets, one deep target, and a 10% first-read share (third on the team behind Drake London and Jahan Dotson). I'm hesitant to plug Pitts back into a lineup this week. Green Bay has held tight ends to the 13th-fewest yards per target while ranking 16th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to the position. I have to see Pitts' usage and production scale up with Michael Penix back or a smash matchup to feel better about Pitts. Sit him this week.

Last week, Hunter Henry saw a big bump in his role. He tied for the team lead in target share and first-read share with 18.2% and 23.1%. He finished with 40 receiving yards (1.90 YPRR), one red zone target, and one deep target. Henry could flirt with TE1 production this week. The Jags have allowed the sixth-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

T.J. Hockenson is the TE15 in fantasy points per game. He has a 20.5% target share, 1.67 YPRR, two red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 16.7% first-read share. Solid usage, but nothing otherworldly. Hockenson was the TE9 in Week 1, and he could flirt with TE1 production this week. Tampa Bay has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Brenton Strange is the TE23 in fantasy points per game. Strange has a 9.6% target share, 1.03 YPRR, two red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 10.5% first-read share. Trevor Lawrence has had eyes for Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. so far this season. I don't see that changing in Week 3 for Strange. New England has held tight ends to the ninth-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Kenyon Sadiq is a wonderful streaming option at the tight end position this week. With Mason Taylor out, I expect Sadiq's role to grow this week. Will Jeremy Ruckert still be involved? Yes, but Sadiq should own the larger portion of a split workload. Sadiq has a 40% route share, a 17% target per route run rate, 1.27 YPRR, zero red zone and deep targets, and an 8.3% first-read share. Ruckert has only had a 20% route share comparatively over the first two games. We could see Sadiq's route share climb into the 60% (or higher) range this week. Detroit is tied for the most tight end touchdowns allowed this season (four). The Lions are 15th in yards per target given up against tight ends while allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Last week, Darren Waller saw his route share increase to 56.4% as he had an 8.3% target share, 33 receiving yards (1.50 YPRR), two red zone targets (two scores), a 13.6% first-read share, and zero deep targets. Waller could see his role grow more this week, but I also wouldn't be shocked to see him utilized in a similar way as Week 2 as well. Waller is a streaming option at tight end this week, facing a defense that ranks 15th in yards per target and has given up the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

I'm approaching this week as if Michael Mayer draws another start in Week 3 for the Raiders. Mayer has been rather unimpressive during his run as the Raiders' starter as the TE21 in fantasy points per game. Mayer has had an 18.5% target share, 1.15 YPRR, one red zone target, zero deep targets, and a 10.5% first-read share. Sit him this week against a pass defense that has allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Aidan Hutchinson was back at it in Week 2, notching two solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Now up to three sacks on the season, Aidan will look to add more to his ledger this week against the New York Jets. Treat Hutchinson as a top-three option for Week 3, thanks to the plus matchup.

Will Anderson was excellent in Week 2, tallying four solos, four assists, one sack, three tackles for loss, and one pass defended against the Cincinnati Bengals. It was the first full sack of the season for Anderson, and the tackle count was great. Count Anderson as a top-five option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Dallas Turner stayed hot in Week 2, tallying three solos, two assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Turner is up to three sacks in two games, propelling him into the top-15 discussion as long as he stays hot. He will have to do just that in Week 3, thanks to a plus matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Turner is playing north of 80 percent of the snaps and is poised for a true breakout season. Start Turner everywhere.

Jeffery Simmons showed up in Week 2, racking up three solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the first of the season for Simmons, but more good times could be on the way in Week 3 with Jameis Winston and the New York Giants on tap. Count Simmons as a top-25 option with top-15 upside, thanks to the plus matchup.

Jaelan Phillips was excellent in Week 1, racking up one solo, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Phillips has recorded a sack in back-to-back weeks for the Panthers and has the fortune of having the Cleveland Browns on the docket for Week 3. Phillips is an easy DL2 play for Week 3 and will carry DL1 upside due to the matchup. Add Phillips in all competitive leagues.

Greg Rousseau continued his blistering start in Week 2, racking up three solos, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble on 68 percent of the snaps. Rousseau is up to four sacks, four tackles for loss, and two forced fumbles through two weeks of the season, elevating him into the DL1 conversation. It doesn't hurt that he has a plus matchup on tap for Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Count Rousseau as part of the top-15 conversation for the Sunday afternoon matchup. Start the Bills pass rusher everywhere; he has entered must-start territory.

Trey Hendrickson showed up in Week 2 for the Baltimore Ravens, racking up three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Hendrickson played just 53 percent of the snaps due to the finger injury, down from the 74 percent he played in Week 1. Mike Green, who notched his first sack of the season, was the biggest beneficiary, seeing his snap share rise from 31 percent to 47 percent. Zion Young also saw a slight bump from 22 to 34 percent. We expect Hendrickson to play more this week, but since he was never much of a run stopper to begin with, this just gives them more of a reason to play the young edges on those downs. Tap Hendrickson as a borderline DL1 option as long as he is playing limited snaps.

DeForest Buckner was rock solid in Week 2, tallying one solo, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Buckner has been lacking in the solo department to open the season, but with 1.5 sacks in two games, who is going to complain? Tap Buckner as a DT1/DL3 option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Houston Texans.

Leonard Williams was back at it in Week 2, tallying four solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Williams has looked excellent to start the season and already has seven solos, three assists, two sacks, and three tackles for loss to his name. Always one of the higher floor DT options due to his tackle upside, Williams becomes a DL2 option when he is rolling. Treat him as such for a plus Week 3 matchup against Washington.

Lukas Van Ness made an impact again in Week 2, this time tallying six solos, three assists, one sack, and three tackles for loss against the New York Jets. LVN led the edge rusher group with 70 percent of the snaps and has likely solidified his role opposite Micah Parsons when the superstar pass rusher returns to the lineup. Van Ness starting the season with a sack in each of his first two games was unexpected, but with Atlanta on tap for Week 3, it would now be a disappointment if he did not extend the streak. Tap Van Ness as a DL3 with matchup-based DL2 upside for a tasty Week 3 matchup against the Falcons and whatever mess they decide to insert under center.

David Bailey was at it again in Week 2, tallying two solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. He played 55 percent of the snaps for the Jets and should continue to see his role expand until he eventually becomes the snap share leader over Will McDonald. Bailey has started his NFL career with a sack in each of his first two games, recording at least five pressures in each. Expect the Jets left edge rusher to be the most sought after name on the wire this week, at least at his position, so be prepared to be aggressive. Tap Bailey as a sack dependent DL2 option for a plus Week 2 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

Nolan Smith continued his hot start to the season in Week 2, recording two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. The sack was just the first of the season for Smith, but he is now up to eight pressures on the season after he added the two from this week to his six against Washington in Week 1. Smith is playing heavy snaps on the edge for Philadelphia with Jonathan Greenard sidelined, seeing 67 and 77 percent of the snaps, respectively, in Week 1 and Week 2. He may see his snaps scaled back drastically when Greenard does return, so keep an eye on his injury status on Friday before determining whether or not to start Smith for Week 3. If he does get the start, he is going to be a borderline DL2 option thanks to an expected matchup against Tyson Bagent and the Chicago Bears.

Mason Graham continued his strong start to the season, racking up one solo, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Graham has a sack in back-to-back games to start the season and is now in the top-five mix at the DT position. His production also puts him in the DL3 mix for Week 3 and beyond, as he has Carolina in Week 3 and then can operate as a bye week filler or DL3 option. An obvious must add in DT leagues, the former fifth overall pick is a solid DL3 add where needed.

Jonathan Allen showed up again in Week 2, racking up three solos, one sack, and three tackles for loss. Now up to a sack in each of his first two games played, Allen has become a pressure monster (seven pressures in Week 2) thanks to playing next to Dexter Lawrence, who commands more attention than him at this point in their respective careers. Allen is a must-start DL3 option as long as he is cooking. Count him as just that for a tasty Week 3 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

A'Shawn Robinson showed out in Week 2, reeling off two solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Robinson is in the DT1 mix given plus matchups like this week's contest against the Minnesota Vikings, but will settle back in as a DT2 for most matchups. He may have some spots during the byes as a DL3 option, but in DL leagues you should look elsewhere outside of them.

Kingsley Enagbare showed up again in Week 2, this time reeling off two solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble on 41 percent of the snaps. Kingsley had a sack in Week 1 as well, making it quite the start for the rotational edge setter. Enagbare is deployed more as a run stuffer on obvious running downs, so his ability to net two sacks in two weeks on 66 and 41 percent of the snaps, respectively, is highly impressive. That said, Kingsley is still not someone managers in 12 team leagues should be deploying for Week 3. The Lions do present a plus matchup, and the streak makes him roster worthy, but his role means you can find better options before the byes begin. Look elsewhere for your Week 3 DL3.

Sheldon Rankins was excellent in Week 2, racking up two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss against the Cincinnati Bengals. Rankins is in the DT2 mix due to a combination of sack upside and his workload in the middle. Rankins played 73.3 percent of the snaps in Week 2 and should continue to dominate snaps in the Texans rotation along the interior of the defensive line. Tap Rankins as a DT2 where needed, but look elsewhere for Week 3 in DL leagues.

Elijah Ponder continues to play heavy snaps (78 percent) on the edge with Harold Landry still sidelined and responded with three solos, two assists, one sack, three tackles for loss, and one fumble recovery. His role alone gives him bench depth upside, but he is not someone you want to be plugging into lineups without byes to force your hand. Keep him rostered, but look elsewhere outside of 20+ team leagues.

Malcolm Roach impressed in Week 2, reeling off three solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Roach played just 48.6 percent of the snaps, good for second on the team, but in a five player interior rotation, it is not going to be enough most weeks for Roach to make enough of an impact to warrant plugging into lineups outside of DT leagues. There is some upside here if his role expands in the future, but for now leave him on the bench for a neutral

Mr. Schwesinger showed up in Week 2, racking up five solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. An LB1 overall candidate in draft season, Carson hasn't quite lived up to the projections through two contests, but the same can be said by more than a few at the position. He has eight solos, 12 assists, and two tackles for loss through two games, so it is not like he has given us LB3 or flex production, but that just serves to accentuate the sky-high upside and expectations for the second year player. Tap Schwesinger as a top-five option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Blake Cashman was excellent in Week 2, notching six solos, four assists, and one sack. Cashman remains one of the most underrated LB1-level producers despite his consistent play year after year. Tap Cashman as a top-15 option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Nick Bolton bounced back from a quiet Week 1 to record six solos, seven assists, and one tackle for loss against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday Night Football. Bolton remains a top-10 option for now, but will need to stay consistent to hold off some of the emerging top-12 options. Count the Chiefs linebacker as a top-10 play for a tasty Week 3 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Alex Singleton impressed again in Week 2, racking up five solos, four assists, and one pass defended. Singleton has 10 solos and 15 assists through two contests, solidifying him as a weekly top-20 option. Treat him as such for a neutral Week 3 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Nakobe Dean was excellent again in Week 2, reeling off seven solos, three assists, and one forced fumble. Dean has recorded at least five solos and a forced fumble in each of his first two contests of the season, pushing his way into the top-15 conversation in the process. Treat him as such for a plus Week 3 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

Edgerrin Cooper was at it again in Week 2, registering six solos, two assists, one sack, and three tackles for loss. Cooper has recorded at least six solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss in each of his first two games, proving that he is a top-15 option for the 2026 season. Treat him as just that for a tasty Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Quay Walker showed up in Week 2, racking up five solos and five assists. Nakobe Dean looks like the one who will be more consistent among the Raiders off-ball linebackers, as Quay drops into coverage more, but there is still room for both in the weekly top-25 discussion. Treat Walker as an upside LB2 for a plus Week 3 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

Azeez Al-Shaair stayed hot in Week 3, tallying six solos and six assists. Azeez played 100 percent of the snaps for the Texans and should continue to soak up tackles for as long as Henry To'oTo'o remains sidelined. Al-Shaair makes for an intriguing LB2 option regardless of opponent. Start him everywhere as an LB2

Jihaad Campbell stayed hot in Week 2, racking up six solos, four assists, and one forced fumble. Jihaad has been producing at a LB1 level through the first two weeks of the season and should be considered an elite LB2 play for a tasty Week 3 matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Payton Wilson was at it again in Week 2, tallying four solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. Wilson has moved his way into the LB2 discussion with his strong start to the season and will be just that for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals. Start Wilson wherever possible.

Demetrius Knight showed up in Week 2, notching four solos and eight assists. The production, while impressive, is a far cry from his monster Week 1, which saw him post five solos, two assists, and a fumble recovery for a touchdown, but it suggests that he is going to settle in as a top-25 to top-30 option this season. Tap him as an elite LB2 play for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Akeem Davis-Gaither went off on Sunday Night Football, reeling off seven solos, seven assists, and one tackle for loss. ADG was a standout in Week 1 as well, with five solos and three assists, meaning he has been one of the hottest linebacker options to start the season. Tap him as an LB2 with top-15 upside for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Houston Texans. ADG is a must-add who is worth grabbing just to block your rival managers. He is going to be good as long as he stays healthy.

Dee Winters was excellent for the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2, tallying seven solos, two assists, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. Winters now has 11 solos through two games, and that is with him leaving this week's contest briefly with a shoulder injury. Winters displayed his LB2 upside with San Francisco last season and looks like he will stay in that conversation as a member of the Cowboys. Treat him as such for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Christian Elliss showed out in Week 2, racking up seven solos, five assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Elliss is going to have his ups and downs this season, but he is playing an everydown role for the Patriots alongside Robert Spillane, putting him squarely in the LB3 mix. Elliss will likely enter the LB2 conversation during the byes (which start next week), making him someone shrewd fantasy managers will want to roster, even if it is just as a depth piece/bye week filler.

Devin Lloyd has been on fire to start the season, most recently exploding for seven solos, two assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, two interceptions, and three passes defended. Lloyd has a standout 16 solos through his first two games, with at least seven in each. The former Jaguars linebacker is showing out without Foyesade Oluokun soaking up tackles, and the shine in pass coverage has propelled him into the LB1 conversation. Treat him as such for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Derrick Barnes was at it again in Week 2, racking up four solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 100 percent of the snaps. If he wasn't before, Barnes has locked himself into the role opposite Jack Campbell, leaving Devn White and Malcolm Rodriguez to soak up WILL snaps when the Lions aren't using nickel looks. Barnes has bullied his way into the LB2 conversation and may not be done yet. For now, treat him as a top-25 option based on his two consecutive LB1-level performances. Add Barnes everywhere.

T.J. Watt was back at it in Week 2, registering two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Now up to three sacks on the season, it is evident that Watt is back to full health and that he is ready to push for the 2026 sack crown. Tap Watt as a top-five option for Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Leo Chenal made an appearance in Week 2, racking up six solos and six assists on 82 percent of the snaps. Chenal saw extra burn with Frankie Luvu (groin) sidelined and should continue to play a near everydown role as long as Luvu is inactive. However, if Luvu is active for Week 3, Chenal will drop back down to the 40 percent range he played in Week 1. This is a situation to monitor, but fantasy managers will want to make other preparations, where possible.

Josiah Trotter cooled down in Week 2 but still put up LB1-level production with five solos and six assists. Already in the record books for his historic Week 1 (first player in NFL history with a sack and a pick-six in their NFL debut), Trotter rarely leaves the field and has jumped into the LB1 discussion due to the explosive start to his rookie season. Treat him as such for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

Bobby Okereke was excellent in Week 2, racking up six solos, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended for the Panthers. Okereke is a solid LB3 play most weeks but becomes an LB2 option for Week 3, thanks to a plus matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Drue Tranquill has been a constant in the Chiefs' linebacking corps and may finally be getting the opportunity to play a near full-time role. Drue logged 87 percent of the snaps in Week 2, racking up four solos, four assists, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Tranquill still profiles as more LB4 than LB3, but with the byes coming, the snap share increase, and plus matchups on the horizon, he can now be treated as a locked-in LB3 candidate. Count him as one for the tasty Week 3 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. Start Tranquill as an LB3 option wherever needed.

Andrew Van Ginkel was at it again in Week 2, reeling off three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Now up to 2.5 sacks on the season, AVG is proving that his fit in Brian Flores' defense is beyond measure. AVG has started hot enough to keep his name in the upside DL2 play discussion, even with the emergence of new names to the weekly discourse. Fire him up as a top-20 option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Pete Werner is splitting time with Danny Stutsman but still managed six solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 53 percent of the snaps. The snap share actually decreased from the 66 percent he saw last week, but some of that can be explained away by New Orleans giving Stutsman extra burn to match the speed of Lamar Jackson. Whatever the case, Werner is not someone you want to risk outside of the flex spot, but as long as he keeps producing, he warrants serious consideration not only for your roster but to be plugged into your lineup. Start him where needed, add him everywhere.

Alex Highsmith was excellent in Week 1, racking up two solos, one assist, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Highsmith has started hot with three sacks in his first two games and is a strong DL3 option for Week 3, thanks to a plus matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals. Start Highsmith everywhere.

Dorian Williams impressed again in Week 2, this time reeling off five solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. His snap share actually dropped from 67 to 57 percent, so that is something to monitor, as the Bills take him off the field in dime looks, something they used on over 25 percent of their defensive plays due to the high-powered Detroit Lions offense being on the other side of the field, playing from behind. That said, with the Los Angeles Chargers being the Week 3 opponent and their offense still a bit of a hot mess, expect the Bills to have Williams on the field for at least 65 percent of the snaps. The fluctuating playing time keeps him in flex territory option wise, but he has proven he is more of an LB3 with LB2 upside based on his first two starts of the season. Start him wherever possible for the plus Week 3 matchup.

Jaishawn Barham impressed in Week 2, racking up four solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss on 63 percent of the snaps. Barham is picking up extra snaps as an off-ball linebacker due to the DeMarvion Overshown injury. Barham has shown some promising potential and has another plus matchup on tap for Week 3 against the Baltimore Ravens, making him worth a start as a flex option in deeper leagues. Start Barham where needed, but roster the rookie third round pick everywhere.

Trenton Simpson showed up in Week 2, racking up five solos, one assist, and one tackle for loss on 62 percent of the snaps. Simpson is playing what looks like a rotational role due to the fact that the Ravens use a three safety look on the bulk of their defensive snaps, with Kyle Hamilton, Malaki Starks, and Jaylinn Hawkins all on the field together. Simpson had been enjoying an expanded role with Teddye Buchanan sidelined, but the starter looks poised to make his return in Week 3. Buchanan avoided the PUP list, so the Ravens may have planned for a Week 3 or Week 4 debut for Teddye from the start. What this means is that Simpson could see his snaps start to dwindle, making him completely untrustworthy outside of the byes and without more adjusted role context. Keep Simpson benched for Week 3, despite the plus matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Look elsewhere for Week 3.

Bradley Chubb showed up in Week 2, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Chubb played just 61 percent of the snaps against the Detroit Lions, down from the 80 percent mark he saw in Week 1. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard intentionally dropped the snap share of his two star edge rushers down in an effort to keep them healthy for the entire season. Chubb is part of the DL2 conversation for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Nick Herbig showed up in Week 1, notching four solos, three assists, three tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Herbig played 53 percent of the snaps and 66 percent in Week 1, so the Steelers' rotation is going to be frequent enough to keep T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, and Herbig all fantasy relevant, especially during the byes. Tap Herbig as a DL3 option thanks to a plus matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Mike Green showed up in Week 2, racking up two solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 47 percent of the snaps. Green saw some extra burn with Trey Hendrickson dealing with a finger injury and parlayed it into the first sack of his season. He played just 31 percent in Week 1, and while he may see his snaps scaled back a bit next week, Hendrickson will not heal for at least four to six weeks, based on most estimated timelines. Treat Green as a bye week piece for now. Leave him on benches for Week 3 where possible.

Kyle Hamilton showed up in Week 2, reeling off seven solos, six assists, and one tackle for loss. Hamilton had a quiet Week 1, but bounced back in DB1 fashion against the New Orleans Saints. Continue to treat him as a top-three option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Budda Baker was excellent in Week 2, racking up seven solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Hamilton has been on a throwback swing for the first two weeks of the season, chipping in 1.5 sacks to go with at least four solos per game. Baker remains a DB2 option, but this is a reminder that he is someone who can lead your team in points at the position, or at all the IDP slots on your roster, on any given week. Count him as a top-20 option for Week 3.

Tykee Smith showed up in Week 2, tallying four solos, one assist, and three tackles for loss. Tykee had a down Week 1 but showed off some of his upside in Week 2. He emerged as a DB1 option last season and will continue to be counted as one for the foreseeable future. Treat him as just that for a tasty Week 3 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

Amani Hooker was excellent in Week 2, notching three solos, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Hooker has had a stronger start to the season than most would have anticipated and enters the top-25 conversation for Week 3 due to a plus matchup against a banged-up New York Giants offense. Tap Hooker as an upside DB3 play going forward.

Xavier Watts bounced back from a quiet Week 1 to record six solos, one assist, and one forced fumble against the Carolina Panthers. Watts has flashed DB1 upside in the past, but can be viewed as more of a DB2 option for the time being. Treat him as such for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Evan Williams was at it again in Week 2, reeling off seven solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. Williams had six solos in Week 1, putting him at 13 in just two contests. This type of solo consistency puts him squarely in the DB2 mix going forward, and especially in Week 3, thanks to a plus matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. The Packers safety deserves to be rostered in all competitive leagues based on his blistering start. Make the add wherever he is available.

Grant Delpit showed up in Week 2, reeling off five solos and one sack. He was quiet in Week 1 and will likely be more inconsistent than his name would suggest. Treat him as a DB3 option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Andrew Wingard showed up again in Week 2, tallying five solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Wingard's strong start to the season puts him in the elite DB3 conversation, and we will be counting him as a DB2 option during the byes. Tap him as a top-30 option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. Wingard is someone who should be rostered in all competitive leagues.

Dax Hill continued his impressive start to the season, racking up four solos, six assists, and four passes defended. Dax has been a DB1-level producer over the first two weeks of the season, and has done so as an outside corner who has yet to record an interception. Suffice it to say that Dax is now in the weekly CB1 overall conversation and belongs in the top-25 DB conversation until he cools down. Treat him as such for a plus matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. Dax should be rostered in all competitive leagues, regardless of whether your league has a CB slot.

Ji'Ayir Brown was excellent in Week 2, tallying four solos, eight assists, and one tackle for loss. Brown played every snap for the 49ers and should continue to offer DB3 value going forward. As his two solo, two assist Week 1 proved, he will be inconsistent, hence the DB3 label, but there is weekly DB2 upside here despite his primarily deep role. Tap him as a top-36 option for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Start him as a DB3 play where needed.

Byron Murphy was excellent in Week 2, tallying four solos, three assists, one interception, and two passes defended. Murphy has had a strong start to the season, reminding IDP managers of why he enters the DB2 conversation during some bye weeks. Locked in as a CB1/DB3 option, Murphy is a top-36 play for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Marcus Sigle was excellent in Week 2, racking up three solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Sigle stood out in Week 1 as well with his four solos and five assists, putting him in the top-25 conversation for Week 3, thanks to a plus matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Sigle should settle in as a DB3, who will have matchup-based DB2 upside during the byes. Add Sigle wherever needed.

Andre Cisco has been making the most of his time in the starting lineup for the New York Jets, most recently notching four solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Cisco has registered at least four solos in each of his first two contests of the season and makes for a solid DB3 option for as long as Minkah Fitzpatrick remains sidelined. Cisco appears to have at least one more start before Minkah returns, so tap the Jets safety as a DB3 option where needed for a plus Week 3 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

Jourdan Lewis showed up in Week 2, racking up four solos, one interception, and one pass defended. Lewis is a CB2 option with CB1 upside but is someone better plugged into lineups in deeper DB leagues. Look elsewhere unless you play in a CB league with two or more starting spots.

Jaden Hicks stepped up for Kansas City in Week 2, racking up five solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. Hicks played every snap for the Chiefs with Chamarri Conner (knee) inactive, up from the 84 percent he played in Week 1. Chamarri returned to the practice field on Wednesday, albeit in a limited fashion, so Hicks will likely drop to a 30-50 percent role when the Chiefs use three safety looks. If you have him rostered, start making contingency plans in case Conner is active for Week 3.

Christian Benford was excellent in Week 2, racking up five solos, three assists, and two passes defended for the Buffalo Bills. Benford is a solid CB2 option but is not someone who should be rostered in 12 team leagues outside of the byes. Look elsewhere for Week 3.

Javon Bullard showed up in Week 1, racking up five solos, two assists, and two tackles for loss on 75 percent of the snaps. Bullard played just 54 percent of the snaps in Week 1, resulting in just one solo as the Packers are using heavy 4-3 looks based on game plan and opposing offensive personnel. The fluctuating snap share is not ideal, as Bullard was already a borderline DB3 play to begin with. Keep him rostered for the byes, but look elsewhere for Week 3.

Eric Stokes showed up on the fantasy radar in Week 2, reeling off two solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble for the Raiders. Stokes is not on the fantasy radar outside of CB leagues at this time. Look elsewhere unless you need CB3 help for Week 3.

Cam Hart was at it again in Week 2, tallying three solos, one assist, one interception, and two passes defended on 84 percent of the snaps. Hart had five solos, one assist, and one pass defended in Week 1, so he has had a strong start for an outside corner. Tap him as an elite CB2 option where needed but wait for the byes before deploying him in DB leagues.

Charles Woods impressed in Week 2, notching eight solos, two assists, and one pass defended on 85.7 percent of the snaps. Woods logged his snaps on the boundary when Marcus Jones kicked inside, providing cover for the injured Carlton Davis. Woods played just one snap in Week 1 (the one snap was when Davis left the field with a stinger (which flared up during the week)), suggesting that he is a special teams only player when Davis is healthy until further notice. Look elsewhere for Week 3 if Davis returns to action as expected.

Myles Harden showed up again in Week 2, reeling off two solos, three assists, one interception, and two passes defended. Despite playing in the slot, Harden is not much of a fantasy option outside of deeper CB leagues due to his sporadic snap share (44 percent in Week 1) and is dealing with a minor shoulder injury that takes him off the radar for Week 3.

The AFC Defensive Player of the Week, the rookie fifth round pick, took full advantage of his start for the injured Darein Porter. Hezekiah Masses exploded in his NFL debut, tallying four solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, two interceptions, and two passes defended on 73.5 percent of the snaps against the Los Angeles Chargers. Masses played zero defensive snaps in Week 1, and with Porter returning to practice, albeit in a limited capacity, on a Wednesday, the veteran is trending in the right direction for Week 3. The upside has proved tantalizing, and he should now be in the rotation, but until he formally steals the job, Masses needs to be left on benches for fantasy.
